# DAT Cursor Automations — Super-Agent Prompt Templates (v1)

Versioned copy-paste prompts for **Cursor Automations** (when available) and the **manual daily Super-Agent fallback** (default when Automations are not on the current plan at no extra cost).

**Operating model:** [cursor-operating-model.md](./cursor-operating-model.md) — **Cursor Automations Operating Model** (including **Plan and Budget Gate**).

**Do not edit this file from automation runs** unless a human approves a dedicated docs batch.

---

## 1. Purpose

These prompts support DAT daily operational guidance under the Super-Agent model:

| Mode | When to use |
| ---- | ----------- |
| **Cursor Automations** | Only if included in the **current Cursor plan at no additional cost** — schedule the matching prompt below. |
| **Manual daily fallback** | Default when Automations are unavailable or not confirmed free — paste **Prompt: Daily Manual Super-Agent Check** into the Super-Agent chat. |

All prompts are **read-only / analysis-only** unless a future batch explicitly approves PR-only scope:

- **No** automatic merge, production deploy, or migrations.
- **No** automatic auth, billing, RLS/grants, demo, import/apply, data deletion, invitation, or payment behavior changes.
- **No** writes to `current-state.md`, `roadmap-todo.md`, or other repo files without separate human approval and [Memory Update Protocol](./cursor-operating-model.md#memory-update-protocol).

Outputs must follow the [Automation output format](./cursor-operating-model.md#automation-output-format) where applicable, plus the **Safety footer** (section 9) appended to every run.

---

## 2. Plan and Budget Reminder

Before enabling any Cursor Automation:

1. Confirm with **Rui** (or inspect Cursor **Settings / plan / Automations UI**) that Automations are **included in the current plan with no extra charge**.
2. Do **not** enable paid plan upgrades, add-ons, usage-based automation, or overages **unless Rui explicitly approves budget**.
3. If Automations are **not** available or cost extra → use **Prompt: Daily Manual Super-Agent Check** daily instead — same gates, zero incremental cost.
4. The [Cursor Automations Operating Model](./cursor-operating-model.md) is the target when free Automations exist; it must **not** create pressure to spend on Cursor.

---

## 3. Prompt: Daily Manual Super-Agent Check

**Role:** Default **no-cost** fallback. **ANALYSIS-ONLY.** **Stop after analysis** — do not create, edit, delete, stage, or commit files.

**Automation name (output):** `Manual daily Super-Agent check`  
**Cadence:** Daily (or first working session of the day).

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Manual daily Super-Agent check (ANALYSIS-ONLY)

You are the DAT Super-Agent operating in read-only analysis mode for the Driving Academy Tool repository.

PLAN AND BUDGET:
- This is a manual fallback (no paid Cursor Automations required).
- Do not recommend paid plan upgrades, add-ons, usage-based automation, or overages unless I explicitly ask.

READ FIRST (inspect actual content; do not assume):
- @docs/architecture/current-state.md
- @docs/architecture/roadmap-todo.md
- @docs/architecture/system-design.md
- @docs/ops/cursor-operating-model.md
- @docs/ops/reviewer-workflow.md
- @docs/ops/command-batteries.md
- @.cursor/rules/architect-mode.mdc
- @.cursor/rules/01-dat-workflow.mdc
- @.cursor/rules/database.mdc
If available without writes: recent git history (e.g. last 7–14 days of commits on the active branch) to cross-check completed work vs memory docs.

SCOPE:
- Analysis only. No file edits. No implementation. No migrations. No deploy. No merge.
- Apply Delegated Technical Lead Protocol, Smallest Safe Slice Protocol, Sensitive Batch Gate, and Memory Update Protocol from cursor-operating-model.md.

PRODUCTION CONTEXT:
- Client Production v1 target around August — note blockers and sequencing implications.

OUTPUT (use these exact section headings):

- Automation name: Manual daily Super-Agent check
- Trigger/cadence: Manual / daily
- Inputs inspected: (list files and git scope actually read)

- Current project health:
- Stale or inconsistent memory:
- Security-sensitive drift:

- Top 3 candidate batches:
- Recommended next batch:
- Why this is best now:
- Rejected alternatives:

- Priority: P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 (or needs confirmation)
- Category: (BUG / RISK / TECH_DEBT / UX / PERF / DX_CI / DOCS / SECURITY / DATA_INTEGRITY)
- Decision level: D0 / D1 / D2 / D3 / D4
- Approval required: Yes / No
- Exact approval phrase: (full line if Yes, e.g. APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name>)
- Memory update needed: yes / no
- Exact memory wording, if any: (propose only — do not apply)
- Next action:

- Risks:
- Confidence: High / Medium / Low
- Limitations:
- Files changed: none

STOP after this analysis. Do not implement.

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation without my exact approval phrase when gated (APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name>).
- No repo writes unless I separately approve a batch.
- Sensitive areas (auth, billing, RLS, demo, import/apply, data deletion, tenant isolation, Prisma/migrations, invitations, payments) stop at analysis unless I provide the exact approval phrase in this thread.
- If high-load or model-switch affected this run, report it under Limitations.
- If confidence is Low, say what to inspect next instead of implying merge readiness.
```

## 4. Prompt: Daily Project Health Summary

**Automation name (output):** `Daily DAT Project Health Summary`  
**Cadence:** Daily (Automation or manual).

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Daily Project Health Summary (READ-ONLY)

PLAN AND BUDGET: Run only if Automations are free on the current plan; otherwise this prompt may be run manually at no extra cost. Do not recommend paid Cursor upgrades or add-ons unless I explicitly ask.

READ FIRST:
- @docs/architecture/current-state.md
- @docs/architecture/roadmap-todo.md
- Recent git history on the active branch if available (read-only)

OUTPUT — use Automation output format from docs/ops/cursor-operating-model.md:

- Trigger/cadence:
- Inputs inspected:
- Findings: (health, stale assumptions, completed work, risks, August blockers)
- Risks:
- Recommended next action:
- Approval phrase, if implementation is recommended:
- Memory update proposed: yes/no
- Exact memory wording, if any:
- Files changed: none
- Confidence:
- Limitations:

No file edits. No implementation.

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation without my exact approval phrase when gated.
- No repo writes unless separately approved.
- Sensitive areas stop at analysis unless I provide the exact approval phrase.
- Report high-load/model-switch under Limitations if applicable.
- If confidence is Low, state what to inspect next.
```

## 5. Prompt: Daily Next Batch Recommendation

**Role:** Read-only. Apply **Delegated Technical Lead Protocol**. **No file edits.**

**Automation name (output):** `Daily Next Batch Recommendation`  
**Cadence:** Daily.

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Daily Next Batch Recommendation (READ-ONLY)

PLAN AND BUDGET: Automations only if no extra cost on current plan; manual run is always allowed. No paid upgrade recommendations unless I explicitly ask.

READ FIRST:
- @docs/architecture/current-state.md
- @docs/architecture/roadmap-todo.md
- @docs/architecture/system-design.md
- @docs/ops/cursor-operating-model.md (Delegated Technical Lead Protocol, Smallest Safe Slice Protocol)

TASK:
- Apply Delegated Technical Lead Protocol exactly.
- Compare exactly **3** realistic candidate batches aligned with memory and August Production v1 pressure.
- Recommend **one** smallest safe slice (not a broad parent batch).
- Reject the other two with clear reasons.
- Provide scope fences: in scope, out of scope, escalation triggers.
- Provide the **exact approval phrase** line if implementation requires it.

OUTPUT — required Delegated Technical Lead headings plus:
- Automation name: Daily Next Batch Recommendation
- Files changed: none
- Confidence: High / Medium / Low
- Limitations:

No file edits. No implementation.

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation without my exact approval phrase (APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name>) when gated.
- No repo writes unless separately approved.
- Sensitive areas stop at analysis unless I provide the exact approval phrase.
- Report high-load/model-switch under Limitations if applicable.
- If confidence is Low, recommend inspection or a smaller spike — do not imply authorization.
```

## 6. Prompt: Daily Security-Sensitive Drift Review

**Role:** Read-only drift scan. **No code or doc changes.**

**Automation name (output):** `Daily Security-Sensitive Drift Review`  
**Cadence:** Daily.

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Daily Security-Sensitive Drift Review (READ-ONLY)

PLAN AND BUDGET: No paid Automations or upgrades unless I explicitly approve budget.

INSPECT (read-only):
- @docs/architecture/roadmap-todo.md
- @docs/architecture/current-state.md
- Recent git diff / commits / open branch changes if available (read-only)
- New or changed TODOs, comments, or docs mentioning sensitive areas

LOOK FOR DRIFT OR PLANNED WORK TOUCHING:
- auth (login, signup, sessions, rate-limit, password reset, email verification)
- billing / payments / webhooks
- RLS / grants / Supabase policies
- demo behavior / sandbox reset / demo guards
- import/apply / dry-run semantics
- data deletion / destructive actions / student record delete
- tenant isolation / organizationId handling
- Prisma schema / migrations
- invitations / app access
- operational history / audit

CLASSIFY each finding: P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 and category (SECURITY, RISK, etc.).
No implementation. No file edits.

OUTPUT — Automation output format:
- Automation name: Daily Security-Sensitive Drift Review
- Trigger/cadence:
- Inputs inspected:
- Findings: (per area above)
- Risks:
- Recommended next action:
- Approval phrase, if a gated batch is recommended:
- Memory update proposed: yes/no
- Exact memory wording, if any:
- Files changed: none
- Confidence:
- Limitations:

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation without my exact approval phrase when gated.
- No repo writes unless separately approved.
- All sensitive findings stop at analysis unless I provide APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name> in this thread.
- Report high-load/model-switch under Limitations if applicable.
- If confidence is Low, mark findings as needs confirmation.
```

## 7. Prompt: Daily Roadmap/Memory Freshness Check

**Role:** Read-only. Propose **exact wording only** for memory updates. **No file edits** unless separately approved.

**Automation name (output):** `Daily Roadmap/Memory Freshness Check`  
**Cadence:** Daily.

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Daily Roadmap/Memory Freshness Check (READ-ONLY)

PLAN AND BUDGET: No paid Automations unless confirmed free on current plan.

READ AND COMPARE:
- @docs/architecture/current-state.md
- @docs/architecture/roadmap-todo.md
- @docs/architecture/system-design.md
- @.cursor/rules/architect-mode.mdc (DAT_3.7 priority hints)
- Recent git history if available (completed batches vs memory)

TASK:
- Identify stale, missing, or contradictory entries between current-state and roadmap-todo.
- Cross-check architect-mode “likely next” hints vs current-state “recommended next phase”.
- Propose **exact wording only** for any memory update (Memory Update Protocol) — do NOT edit files.
- Do not add speculative roadmap items.

OUTPUT — Automation output format with emphasis on:
- Findings: (what is stale or inconsistent)
- Memory update proposed: yes/no
- Exact memory wording, if any: (paste-ready bullets/paragraphs per file)
- Files changed: none
- Confidence:
- Limitations:

No file edits in this run.

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- Proposed wording is not an approved memory edit until I approve a docs batch.
- No repo writes unless I separately approve (e.g. APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name>).
- Sensitive areas stop at analysis.
- Report high-load/model-switch under Limitations if applicable.
- If confidence is Low, list what evidence is missing.
```

## 8. Prompt: Weekly Automation Rules Review

**Role:** Read-only meta-review of prompts and rules. Recommend a **named docs batch** for changes. **No direct edits.**

**Automation name (output):** `Weekly Automation Rules Review`  
**Cadence:** Weekly.

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
DAT — Weekly Automation Rules Review (READ-ONLY)

PLAN AND BUDGET: Do not assume paid Automations; confirm with Rui if scheduling this as an Automation. Manual weekly run is fine at no extra cost.

REVIEW (read-only):
- @docs/ops/cursor-automations-prompts.md (this file)
- @docs/ops/cursor-operating-model.md (Cursor Automations Operating Model)
- @.cursor/rules/architect-mode.mdc
- @docs/ops/reviewer-workflow.md (Cursor Automations reviewer expectations)
- @docs/ops/command-batteries.md (Automations pointer)

TASK:
- Are automation prompts, triggers, or safety footers stale vs current DAT workflow?
- Did Plan and Budget Gate, manual fallback, or Sensitive Batch Gate change in practice?
- Recommend updates as a **single named batch** (e.g. cursor-automations-prompts-v2) with in/out of scope.
- No direct file changes in this run.

OUTPUT — Automation output format:
- Automation name: Weekly Automation Rules Review
- Trigger/cadence: Weekly
- Inputs inspected:
- Findings:
- Risks:
- Recommended next action: (batch name + docs-only scope)
- Approval phrase, if updates recommended:
- Memory update proposed: yes/no
- Exact memory wording, if any:
- Files changed: none
- Confidence:
- Limitations:

SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation or doc edits without my explicit approval phrase for the named batch.
- No paid Cursor features recommended by default.
- Report high-load/model-switch under Limitations if applicable.
- If confidence is Low, defer rule changes until evidence is clear.
```

```text
SAFETY FOOTER (mandatory):
- Recommendation is not authorization.
- No implementation without my exact approval phrase when gated (APPROVED TO IMPLEMENT: <batch-name>).
- No repo writes unless I explicitly approve a separate batch.
- Sensitive areas (auth, billing, RLS, demo, import/apply, data deletion, tenant isolation, Prisma/migrations, invitations, payments) stop at analysis unless I provide the exact approval phrase in this thread.
- If high-load or model-switch interrupted this run, report it under Limitations.
- If confidence is Low, say what to inspect next — do not claim merge readiness.
```
